name: CORAL
tagline: University of Wisconsin deductive database (1988–1997) that mixed declarative Horn-clause rules with C++.
description: CORAL was a deductive database system developed at the University of Wisconsin–Madison by Raghu Ramakrishnan, Divesh Srivastava, S. Sudarshan and Praveen Seshadri, among others. Programs are organised as modules of Horn-clause rules extended with complex terms, set-grouping, aggregation, negation and relations containing variables, and the system picked an evaluation strategy per module automatically while letting users steer optimisation with per-module control annotations. A C++ interface let developers combine declarative modules with imperative code and extend the system through C++ classes. Data could live in memory or on disk through the EXODUS storage manager, which also supplied client-server transactions. The final release, 1.5.2, came out in November 1997; it remains a well-cited reference for Datalog evaluation techniques.
statusNote: Academic project (1988–1997); final release 1.5.2 in Nov 1997. Its techniques continue in modern Datalog engines.

license.name: Academic source release (no OSI license stated)

pricing.notes: Source and 1990s Unix binaries still downloadable from the project page.

strengths: Rich declarative language: Horn clauses with complex terms, aggregation, set-grouping and negation
Chooses an evaluation strategy per module, with user-controllable optimisation
Tight C++ integration for mixing declarative and imperative code
Handled both main-memory and disk-resident relations
weaknesses: Unmaintained since 1997; builds target 1990s Unix toolchains
useCases: Studying deductive database and Datalog evaluation techniques
Historical reference for recursive query processing
